body.p: This listing of claims will replace all prior versions, and listings, of claims in the application:

br.br:
1-10. (Canceled)29
11. (Previously Presented) A smart garment for detecting physiological data of a user, the smart garment comprising:a garment configured to be worn on an upper body of the user,
a plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes, wherein each of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes comprises interlaced conductive fibers for conducting a plurality of ECG signals with respect to the upper body of the user while in contact with skin of the user;
wherein the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes includes a textile-based ECG electrode pairing comprising at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode for transmitting a controller-generated signal generated by a controller device through the skin of the user, and at least one textile-based ECG receiver electrode, spaced apart from the textile-based ECG generator electrode, for sensing the controller-generated signal through the skin of the user,
the controller device electronically coupled to the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes, the controller device configured to:
generate the controller-generated signal,
transmit the controller-generated signal through the at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode,
sense the controller-generated signal from the at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode via the at least one textile-based ECG receiver electrode,
based on sensing the controller-generated signal, generated by the controller device, and transmitted by the at least one textile-based ECG receiver electrode:
determine that the at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode and/or the at least one textile-based ECG receiver electrode of the textile-based ECG electrode pairing (i) is at least partially out of contact with the skin of the user and/or (ii) causes the controller-generated signal that is transmitted through the at least one of the textile-based ECG generator electrode to be of unacceptable signal quality,
deselect the at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode and/or the at least one textile-based ECG receiver electrode of the textile-based ECG electrode pairing, and select another textile-based ECG electrode pairing, and
repeat said generating of the controller-generated signal and said sensing of the controller-generated signal using the another textile-based ECG electrode pairing.
12. (Currently Amended) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the controller device determines a percentage of contact surface area of one or more of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes with the skin of the user.
13. (Currently Amended) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the controller device detects whether one or more of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes are in acceptable contact with the skin of the user.
14. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, further comprising monitoring a signal quality of the controller-generated signal and repeating deselecting the determined textile- based ECG electrode and selecting a different textile-based ECG electrode as a result of said monitoring.
15. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the interlaced conductive fibers comprise conductive yarns.
16. (Currently Amended) The smart garment of claim 15, wherein the conductive yarns are knitted into at least one of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes.
17. (Currently Amended) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the controller device determines a change in a desired location of one or more of the plurality of the textile-based ECG electrodes.
18. (Currently Amended) The smart garment of claim 11, further comprising a plurality of the textile-based ECG generator electrodes and a plurality of the textile-based ECG receiver electrodes.
19. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 18, wherein the controller-generated signal is generated using a given generator electrode of the plurality of textile-based ECG generator electrodes and the controller-generated signal is sensed using a given receiver electrode of the plurality of textile-based ECG receiver electrodes.
20. (Currently Amended) The smart garment of claim 19, wherein the controller device is configured to determine whether the controller-generated signal generated using the given generator electrode and the controller-generated signal sensed using the given receiver electrode does not satisfy a signal quality threshold, and selects an alternative generator electrode and/or an alternative receiver electrode.
21. (Currently Amended) The smart garment of claim 20, wherein the controller device continues selecting alternative generator electrodes and/or alternative receiver electrodes to choose a generator electrode and receiver electrode pairing that satisfies a-thesignal quality threshold.
22. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the garment includes a belt portion having at least one of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes.
23. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the interlaced conductive fibers are formed by weaving electrically conductive threads.
24. (Currently Amended) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the controller device uses physiological data sensed by the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes to determine a quantity of the user selected from the group consisting of: a PR interval, a QT interval, a corrected QT (QTc) interval, a PR axis, and a QRS axis.
25. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the plurality of textile- based ECG electrodes are exposed on a first side and insulated on a second side.
26. (Currently Amended) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the interlaced conductive fibers are interlaced with non-conductive fibers of a body of the smart garment.
27. (Currently Amended) The smart garment of claim 11, further comprising a conductive trace connected to the each of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes, each of the conductive traces for connecting the pluralityof textile-based ECG electrodes to the controller device for sending and receiving one or more electronic signals using the plurality of textile- based ECG electrodes.
28. (Currently Amended) The smart garment of claim 27, wherein the controller device alternates different pairings chosen from the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes as one or more selected pairs in order to determine a decided optimum signal from the one or more electronic signals received from the different pairings.
29. (Currently Amended) A smart garment for detecting physiological data of a user, the smart garment comprising:a plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes, wherein each of the plurality of textile- based ECG electrodes comprises interlaced conductive fibers for conducting a plurality of ECG signals with respect to a body of the user;
wherein the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes includes at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode for transmitting a controller-generated signal generated by a controller device through the user's skin, and at least one textile-based ECG receiver electrode spaced apart from the textile-based ECG generator electrode for sensing the controller-generated signal through the user's skin, wherein the textile-based ECG generator electrode that generates the controller-generated signal and the textile-based ECG receiver electrode that senses the controller-generated signal define a textile-based ECG electrode pairing,
the controller device electronically coupled to the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes, the controller device configured to:
generate the controller-generated signal,
transmit the controller-generated signal through the at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode,
sense the controller-generated signal via one or more textile-based ECG receiver electrodes,
based on the sensing the controller-generated signal generated by the controller device:
determine at least one of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes from the textile-based ECG electrode pairing (i) is at least partially out of contact with skin of the user the user's skin and/or (ii) causes the controller- generated signal that is transmitted through the at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode to be of unacceptable signal quality,
deselect the at least one determined textile-based ECG electrode from the electrode pairing, and select another textile-based ECG electrode pairing, and repeat said generate the controller-generated signal and said sense of the controller-generated signal using the another textile-based ECG electrode pairing.
30. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the controller device is configured to process the controller-generated signal to analyze the physiological data to determine a defined health event of the user.
